headline: Transcriptomic and machine-learning pipelines nominate candidate disease biomarkers
label: Multi Omics Biomarker Discovery
summary: Public omics resources and single-cell data now routinely yield ML-prioritized candidate genes that still require experimental confirmation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is an integrative workflow that pairs public transcriptomic datasets from GEO and other repositories with WGCNA, machine-learning hub-gene selection, and single-cell RNA-seq to prioritize candidate genes. Several studies add genetic or causal layers: Mendelian randomization and colocalization in the AIF1 and EPAS1 analyses, MAGMA GWAS in the APS-carotid study, and single-cell eQTL mapping in head and neck cancer. Exposure-oriented work extends this frame to environmental agents, linking lead exposure to HMOX1 in colorectal cancer and aflatoxin B1 to RXRB and F11 in nephrotoxicity, while SHAP-interpretable ML integrates exposures and multi-omics in COPD-lung cancer comorbidity. Newer elements include experimental validation of candidates, including EPAS1 in acute myocardial infarction, a SOCS1/SOCS2/GADD45G signature in mice, and EIF6-linked NOX2 signaling in osteoarthritis. Evidence is largely computational, and the nominated candidates require experimental confirmation.
